title: Buttery Mumbai pav bhaji from scratch 🧈🔥 #shorts
dish_fact: Pav bhaji was invented in 1850s Mumbai as a fast, filling meal for textile-mill workers - the soft 'pav' bread is a Portuguese legacy, and the whole dish is cooked and mashed on one big flat iron griddle.

segments.moment_description: Bright village kitchen-garden morning: the young woman fills a basket with potatoes, a small cauliflower, ripe red tomatoes, a green capsicum and a handful of peas, dew and warm sunlight on the vegetables, Studio Ghibli anime screenshot, Hayao Miyazaki style, 2D hand-drawn animation cel, flat cel-shaded colors, visible ink linework
On a wooden board she quickly dices onions, tomatoes and capsicum into tiny pieces and crushes ginger, garlic and green chilli, a satisfying rhythmic close-up of the chopping knife
Boiled potatoes, cauliflower florets and peas steam in a pot; her hand mashes them roughly with a potato masher into a soft chunky mash, steam rising in the cozy kitchen light

A big flat black iron tawa over the fire: a thick slab of butter melts and foams, then the chopped onions, ginger-garlic and tomatoes sizzle with a heaped spoon of deep-red pav bhaji masala, turning into a glossy dark-red gravy, steam and bubbles

The potato-vegetable mash is folded into the red masala on the tawa and mashed together, a fresh knob of butter melting and swirling on top, a shower of chopped coriander, close-up of the bubbling bhaji

Two soft pav buns are split and toasted golden in butter on the side of the tawa, then everything is plated on a leaf plate - buttery bhaji topped with raw onion, a lemon wedge and coriander, the pav beside it, the mouthwatering reveal
